text:
Colton Dach grew up in Fort Saskatchewan, just outside Edmonton, and the Edmonton Journal has called him "the poster boy for upward mobility." The former Blackhawks second-round pick scored twice against the Rangers on Nov. 1, has three goals in 13 games, and Oilers Nation described him as "a menace" on the wing. He's day-to-day now and could return soon.

The physical game is the point. He has 29 hits in 13 games, and his ice time jumped by about three minutes a night over his last ten. That's a coach telling you he trusts him.

The underlying numbers are more cautious. Edmonton has taken just 41% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about 11 points worse than without him, and Evolving-Hockey's numbers last season said offense isn't his game, though his Chicago teammates were in the bottom 6% by impact. Forwards picked in his range average 0.29 points a game in their first full season; he's around there. Our range has him at 10 to 21 goals over a full season. Oilers Nation wondered if he's another reclamation home run. Not yet, but the role is real.
headline: Dach, the local reclamation project
